extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties to PTAB AIA trials (petitioners, patent owners, and their counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for initiating and litigating AIA trials (IPR, PGR, CBM) before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, covering eligibility, filing requirements, institution standards, evidence, hearings, and post-decision options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties to AIA trials — petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner = third party. Files challenge against a patent. Carries legal burdens throughout proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A member of the public who is not the patent owner can file a petition challenging the patentability of an issued patent. If a patent owner sues a party in district court for infringement, that party may bring a petition at the PTAB challenging the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties to AIA trials — patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner has several opportunities to represent their interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may file a preliminary response, file a response after institution, submit evidence (e.g., declarations), file motions to amend, sur-replies, request hearings, and pursue post-decision options such as rehearing, appeal, reissue, or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of AIA trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review (IPR); Post grant review (PGR); Covered business method review (CBM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different trial types have different timing windows and permissible grounds for challenge (see separate criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability windows — IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: from 9 months after patent grant throughout the life of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR may not be instituted if the petition is filed more than 1 year after service of an infringement complaint by the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy (35 U.S.C. § 315(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability windows — PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: PGR: from patent grant through 9 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR is only available during the post-grant window up to nine months after grant; PGR permits broader grounds than IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability windows — CBM
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM: same as PGR, but must be a 'covered business method' patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered business method patent claims a method or corresponding apparatus for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service, and does not include 'technological inventions'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds in petition — IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: only on § 102 and § 103 grounds, and only on basis of prior art consisting of patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR challenges are limited to novelty and obviousness based on patents and printed publications; other invalidity grounds are not available in IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grounds in petition — PGR/CBM
rubrics_metrics.description: PGR/CBM: on any grounds for invalidity (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR and CBM allow challenges on broader statutory and procedural grounds, with the exception of best mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must identify: each claim that it is challenging; the basis for the challenge (known as the 'grounds'); the evidence that supports each ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are grounded in 35 U.S.C. §§ 311, 312(a)(3) and are essential for the PTAB to evaluate institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year time bar for IPR (35 U.S.C. § 315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review may not be instituted if the petition requesting the proceeding is filed more than 1 year after the date on which the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy of the petitioner is served with a complaint alleging infringement of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must check for prior suits and service dates to avoid statutory time bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition (optional) to persuade the PTAB not to institute a trial based on the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response may be based on merits (arguing petition evidence or reasoning is insufficient), time bar, or Board's discretion. It is due no later than 3 months from the date that the PTAB issues a Notice According a Filing Date to the petition. Sources: 35 U.S.C. §§ 313, 315(a)(1), (b), (e)(1), 325(d); 37 CFR 42.107(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's discretion and statutory factors for denying institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Three statutes: 35 U.S.C. ___ — 314(a), 316(b), 325(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 314(a): Director 'may' institute a review — Board considers factors like number/timing of petitions and judicial economy. 316(b): effect on the efficient administration of the Office and ability to timely complete proceedings. 325(d): petition raises the same or substantially the same art or arguments previously considered by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on institution timing
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB will issue a decision on whether to institute a trial within 3 months of the preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB will decide whether the petition has established that the standard for instituting review is met; if yes, PTAB may institute a trial. Source: 35 U.S.C. § 314.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for initiating review — IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: IPR: 'a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail' with respect to at least one challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a lower institution threshold than 'more likely than not' and applies specifically to IPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for initiating review — PGR/CBM
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM/PGR: 'more likely than not that at least one claim is unpatentable' or the petition raises 'a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR/CBM institution uses a higher preponderance-type threshold or permits institution for important unsettled legal questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order and case management
rubrics_metrics.description: If PTAB institutes a trial, it will issue a scheduling order, with a list of due dates for the remaining papers and a hearing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB may revise scheduling orders depending on motions filed; parties may agree to move certain dates; any party may request an initial conference call with PTAB to discuss the schedule. Source: Trial Practice Guide and its update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding timeline and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Phases: First Phase: Institution; Second Phase: Trial. Typical timing: 6 months (institution phase?), 12 months (trial), with a 6 month good cause extension possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall statutory and regulatory timing aims to resolve matters within set windows, but good cause extensions are available in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof at trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is lower than the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard required to prevail in district courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence responsibility and available tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner and patent owner should support their positions with evidence and are responsible for obtaining their own evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools for obtaining evidence include declarations, discovery, and depositions (Source: 37 CFR 42.51(b)(1)(ii), (b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration is a written witness statement made under penalty of perjury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations are commonly used to present factual support; parties may file multiple declarations at specified stages (e.g., petition, reply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and confidentiality issues
rubrics_metrics.description: During discovery, each side may ask the other side to produce evidence in their possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery can become complicated if parties disagree about scope or whether information is confidential or privileged; both sides typically request information from the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions and cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposition is an out-of-court proceeding where a witness gives sworn testimony; during depositions, a party may cross-examine a witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositions allow live examination outside hearing; deposition transcripts may be filed at specific stages as limited new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, patent owner may file a response to the petition (and to the PTAB’s Institution Decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner typically files evidence in support of its position (e.g., a declaration). See Trial Practice Guide and Appendix D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may amend its claims during the trial phase to narrow the scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases, the Board may cancel original claims but conclude that amended claims can be obtained. Additional guidance is in the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide and related notices (e.g., pilot program on Motions to Amend).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner reply stage — new evidence permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may file a reply to patent owner response and may still enter new evidence at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an example, petitioner may file a second declaration at this time. Sources: Scheduling Order; Trial Practice Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner sur-reply — evidentiary restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a sur-reply to petitioner’s reply, but no new evidence may be filed at this time other than a deposition transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If counsel for patent owner have cross-examined the petitioner’s witness about the contents of a second declaration, the deposition transcript may be filed at this time. Sources: Scheduling Order; TPG Update at 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, PTAB will generally hold an oral hearing; parties must request a hearing; date appears in scheduling order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearings may be held in Alexandria, Virginia or regional offices; pilot program allows remote viewing from regional offices. For inventor live testimony at hearing, inventor must previously have submitted a declaration with the Patent Owner Response and/or Motion to Amend, and the panel must authorize live testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB will issue a final written decision for all trials that are instituted, unless there is a termination (settlement). PTAB will rule on the patentability of each claim — uphold or find a claim unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PTAB finds claims to be unpatentable, it will order cancellation of those claims, meaning those claims will not be enforceable anymore. Source: 35 U.S.C. § 318.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision options — rehearing and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The party adversely affected by a final written decision may request that PTAB reconsider a decision or file a timely appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for rehearing are for matters the Board believes were overlooked or misapprehended. Sources: 37 CFR 42.71(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision options — reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may avail themselves of a reissue application or a request for reexamination before, during, or after an AIA trial concludes with a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may proceed after the Board issues a final written decision relating to the same patent under certain circumstances (e.g., timely filed and raises issues different than those previously considered). See Notice regarding options for reissue or reexamination and related Federal Register notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing trial papers and page/word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties file papers using PTAB End-to-End (E2E). PTAB rules set page limits, or in some cases, word count limits on papers filed in an AIA trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB E2E (https://ptab.uspto.gov/#/login) and the PTAB E2E electronic filing guide explain filing procedures. PTAB E2E is different than EFS-Web (used for appeal filings). Sources: 37 CFR 42.6, 42.24.
